metadata.description:
The Government of India, especially Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has been strongly advocating GI tags for tribal products. But does a GI tag by itself really make a difference for tribal communities? Perhaps not.
A GI tag matters only when it is used to create opportunities, build markets, and empower the people behind the product.
Bodoland is a remarkable example of this.
After securing GI tags for 21 tribal products, the community didn’t stop at recognition. Their leaders took proactive steps to turn this achievement into real benefits for artisans, farmers, and tribal women:
This story demonstrates that a GI tag is not merely a certificate, but a powerful tool for transforming local economies—when communities know how to utilise it strategically.
Bodoland proves that recognition is just the beginning; real impact comes from action.
